# Implementation Plan: E-Commerce Platform

**Branch**: `001-ecommerce-platform` | **Date**: 2025-11-09 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-ecommerce-platform/spec.md`

**Note**: This file is generated by the `/speckit.plan` command.

## Summary

Build a full-stack e-commerce web application enabling customers to browse products, manage shopping carts, complete purchases with secure payment processing, and manage user accounts. Administrators can manage products, orders, and view analytics. The platform prioritizes user experience, security, accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), and performance (Lighthouse > 90).

**Technical Approach**: Next.js 15 App Router with React Server Components for server-first architecture, PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM for data persistence, NextAuth.js for authentication, Stripe for PCI-compliant payment processing, and Vercel for deployment with built-in performance optimizations.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.x with strict mode enabled (Next.js 15 runtime)
**Primary Dependencies**: Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19, Prisma 5.x, NextAuth.js 5.x, Stripe SDK, Zod, React Hook Form, TanStack Query, Zustand, shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion
**Storage**: PostgreSQL 15+ (via Supabase or Neon), Cloudinary or AWS S3 for images with CDN
**Testing**: Vitest (unit), React Testing Library (component), Playwright (E2E), c8 (coverage)
**Target Platform**: Web application (mobile-first responsive), deployed on Vercel edge network
**Project Type**: Web (Next.js full-stack with App Router)
**Performance Goals**:
- LCP < 2.5s, FID < 100ms, CLS < 0.1 (Core Web Vitals)
- Page load < 3s, interactions < 1s
- Support 1,000 concurrent users (normal), 10,000 (peak sales events)
- Lighthouse score > 90 on all pages

**Constraints**:
- WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility compliance mandatory
- PCI DSS compliance via Stripe (no raw card data handling)
- GDPR/CCPA data privacy compliance
- Mobile-first responsive design required
- Progressive enhancement (works without JavaScript)
- Security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
- Rate limiting on authentication endpoints

**Scale/Scope**:
- Initial: 100-1,000 products, 100 orders/day
- Growth: 10,000+ products, 1,000+ orders/day
- 6 user stories (P1-P4 priority)
- 82 functional requirements
- 12 data entities

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### ✅ I. User-Centric Design
- **Compliance**: PASS
- **Evidence**:
  - Mobile-first responsive design in requirements (FR-078)
  - WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility (FR-079, FR-080, FR-081)
  - Performance budgets defined (FR-075, FR-076)
  - Success criteria include Lighthouse > 90 (SC-001 through SC-007)
  - Progressive Web App capabilities planned
- **Action**: Continue with mobile-first Tailwind CSS implementation and accessibility testing

### ✅ II. Security & Privacy First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- **Compliance**: PASS
- **Evidence**:
  - PCI DSS via Stripe integration (FR-035, FR-037, FR-072)
  - Input validation with Zod schemas (FR-068)
  - NextAuth.js for secure authentication (FR-009)
  - HTTPS encryption (FR-066, FR-067)
  - Rate limiting (FR-069)
  - GDPR/CCPA compliance (FR-073, FR-074)
  - Security event logging (FR-071)
  - No client-side secrets (constitution mandate)
- **Action**: Implement Zod validation on all inputs, configure NextAuth.js with HTTP-only cookies, setup Stripe webhooks with signature verification

### ✅ III. Test-Driven Development (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- **Compliance**: PASS
- **Evidence**:
  - Vitest for unit tests specified
  - React Testing Library for component tests
  - Playwright for E2E tests
  - Coverage requirements: 80% business logic, 100% payment/security
  - Test-first workflow documented in constitution
- **Action**: Write tests before implementation, setup test data factories with Prisma, configure coverage thresholds in vitest.config.ts

### ✅ IV. Performance & Scalability
- **Compliance**: PASS
- **Evidence**:
  - Next.js 15 RSC for optimized data fetching
  - Image optimization via Next.js Image component (FR-077)
  - Core Web Vitals targets defined (SC-005, SC-006, SC-007)
  - Prisma connection pooling configured
  - Vercel Edge Network CDN for static assets
  - ISR for product pages planned
  - Scalability targets: 1,000-10,000 concurrent users (SC-013, SC-014)
- **Action**: Implement RSC data fetching, configure Next.js Image with blur placeholders, setup ISR revalidation for product catalog

### ✅ V. Modular Architecture
- **Compliance**: PASS
- **Evidence**:
  - Domain modules identified: User Management, Product Catalog, Shopping Cart, Order Management, Payment Processing, Inventory, Admin
  - Next.js App Router with route groups: (auth), (shop), (dashboard)
  - Collocated components with routes
  - Services layer for business logic
  - 12 distinct data entities with clear boundaries
- **Action**: Organize codebase per App Router conventions, create service modules in /lib, maintain clear domain boundaries

### ✅ VI. Server-First Architecture (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- **Compliance**: PASS
- **Evidence**:
  - React Server Components by default
  - Server Actions for mutations (form submissions, cart operations)
  - Progressive enhancement (FR-082: works without JavaScript)
  - Client components only for interactivity (cart updates, search autocomplete)
  - Data fetching in Server Components
- **Action**: Mark components "use client" only when necessary, use Server Actions for all mutations, implement progressive form submission

### 📋 Technology Stack Compliance
- **Compliance**: PASS
- **Mandated Stack**:
  - ✅ Next.js 15 with App Router
  - ✅ TypeScript with strict mode

  - ✅ Zustand for global state, Context for scoped state
  - ✅ TanStack Query for client-side data fetching
  - ✅ React Hook Form + Zod validation
  - ✅ PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM
  - ✅ NextAuth.js for authentication
  - ✅ Stripe for payments
  - ✅ Cloudinary/S3 for file storage

  - ✅ Vercel for deployment
  - ✅ Supabase/Neon for database hosting
  - ✅ Sentry for error monitoring

**Structure Decision**: Selected Next.js 15 App Router structure with route groups for logical organization. The `(auth)`, `(shop)`, and `(dashboard)` route groups provide clean URL structure while maintaining separate layouts for different user contexts. Server Components by default with Client Components marked explicitly for interactivity. Business logic separated into services layer, with Server Actions for mutations to maintain server-first architecture per constitution.
